description:
Calm Evening Music | Slow Sarod | Indian Classical

The week is almost over. You made it to the quiet end of it.

This is the part of Sunday where nothing else needs to happen. The week is closing the door behind it, slowly, and you don't have to do anything to help it along. Just sit, and let the Sarod do the settling. Its notes are deep and rounded, and they slide into each other without any edges — exactly the kind of sound that loosens the shoulders after a long stretch of days.

This is 90 minutes of slow Sarod in Raga Bhupali — a serene, pentatonic evening raga, light and peaceful, with no sharp turns. It isn't sleep music and it isn't trying to fix anything. It's just a calm place to land before the new week begins.

Play it while you tidy up, while you sit with the last of the evening, or while you let Sunday quietly become Monday.

🎵 What you'll hear:
- Sarod — deep, glassy, resonant plucked strings with long sliding sustain
- Raga Bhupali — a serene pentatonic evening raga, peaceful and unhurried
- Soft tanpura drone underneath, holding the calm
- Light, sparse tabla kept very low — presence without momentum
- 90 unbroken minutes at 432Hz tuning

⏱ Chapters
0:00    Settling in — the week winding down
20:00   Letting the shoulders drop
45:00   Quiet and serene
70:00   Calm before the week turns
85:00   Gentle close

🧠 How to use:
Press play and stop reaching for things. Let the Sarod's slow slides set the pace and let the evening get quiet around it. No effort required — just let the week end.

⏱ Best for:
• Sunday evening wind-down
• Settling after a long week
• Quiet evenings with no plans
• Slow reading or tidying before bed
• Letting the day close without rushing into the next one

production_spec.loop_seam: 10s in / 30s out, Suno extend 3-4x → loop in post to fill 90 min
production_spec.notes: Raga Bhupali — serene pentatonic (audava) evening raga. Sa Re Ga Pa Dha Sa — only five notes, NO Ma and NO Ni. The absence of the 4th and 7th gives it an open, light, peaceful character with no tension or sharp resolution — ideal for end-of-week calm. TABLA: light tabla is fine for Sarod, but keep it VERY low and sparse here — this is evening calm, not energetic; tabla should add quiet presence, not momentum. If in doubt, drop it entirely. Soft tanpura drone holds the floor. Theta 5Hz binaural — deep relaxation without pushing toward sleep (this is settling, not sleep music). LUFS -15 (evening calm, slightly quieter than morning-active). EMOTIONAL TAG ROTATION (3 metaphors, one per clip): clip 1: 'like the week quietly closing the door behind it' · clip 2: 'the shoulders finally dropping after a long stretch of days' · clip 3: 'Sunday becoming Monday without any rush'. 90min = 3-4 Suno clips + loop extension. NOTE: this is a DIFFERENT raga and DIFFERENT lane from the June 2 Sarod (Ahir Bhairav, morning-cognitive/clear-head) — this is Bhupali, evening-calm/Sunday wind-down.
